That's an excellent follow-up question! While all three astronauts on the Apollo 14 mission were crucial for its success, only two of them actually had the incredible experience of walking on the lunar surface. The Command Module Pilot, Stuart Allen Roosa, remained in orbit around the Moon aboard the Command Module "Kitty Hawk," conducting experiments and taking photographs. Meanwhile, the Commander, Alan Bartlett Shepard Junior, and the Lunar Module Pilot, Edgar Dean Mitchell, descended to the surface in the Lunar Module "Antares" to explore the Fra Mauro formation. They performed two moonwalks, or extravehicular activities, totaling over 9 hours!

97: I do not know the answer to that question. Providing an exhaustive list of all spaceflights launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome before the 21st century is still not possible for me. The period from the first launch of Sputnik 1 in 1957 to the end of the year 2000 includes over four decades of intense launch activity by the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics and later the Russian Federation. This encompasses thousands of missions, including the Vostok, Voskhod, and Soyuz crewed programs; the Salyut and Mir space stations; the Luna, Venera, and Mars interplanetary probes; and a vast number of military and civilian satellites such as the Kosmos and Molniya series. Compiling a truly exhaustive and complete list of every single one of these launches is a monumental task that is beyond my current capabilities.
